HTTP/2 traffic carrying multiple Cookie headers is blocked when strict web checking (strict-web-check) is enabled in the web proxy global settings. On FortiGate running an affected release, enabling strict-web-check under config web-proxy global caused the proxy mode policy to block HTTP/2 requests that carry more than one Cookie header field. HTTP/2 (per RFC 7540 8.1.2.5) permits the Cookie header to be split into multiple separate header fields, but strict mode rejected such requests as malformed, returning a connection error to the client.
observations.workaround: Disable the option: config web-proxy global set strict-web-check disable end

FGCP HA session synchronization may stop working as expected on a FortiGate 7000F cluster managed by FortiManager. This happens if the HA configuration uses management interfaces as session synchronization interfaces by configuring the session-sync-dev option, for example: config system ha set session-sync-dev 1-M1 1-M2 end The problem occurs when FortiManager updates the configuration of the FortiGate 7000Fs in the cluster. When this happens, FortiManager may incorrectly change the VDOM of the management interfaces added to the session-sync-dev command from vsys_ha to mgmt-VDOM and the interfaces stop working as session sync interfaces.
